title: Huma Qureshi Is India's First Desi Hitwoman. And She's Coming for Alia Bhatt's Opening Weekend.
excerpt: The Baby Do Die Do teaser just dropped — a deaf-mute assassin with a red umbrella, a neo-noir world dripping with mystery, and a July 3 release date that puts her in direct combat with Alpha.
body:
There's a shot in the Baby Do Die Do teaser where Huma Qureshi stands in a parking lot, perfectly still, hair pulled back, eyes unreadable. Two men are talking about her in hushed, nervous tones — about Baby KarMarKar, the woman who vanished. And then she picks up a rifle.

That's the whole pitch. That's the promise. And it lands harder than it has any right to.

The teaser for Huma Qureshi's most unconventional role dropped on Monday, and it does something most Bollywood teasers don't bother with — it creates an atmosphere. Baby KarMarKar is introduced as India's first on-screen desi female assassin. She is deaf-mute. She is lethal. She carries a bright red umbrella through the rain at Badlapur railway station like she's walking into a painting, not a crime scene. She's not a spy with a designer wardrobe and a government mandate. She's something stranger, rawer, and considerably more dangerous.

Directed by Nachiket Samant and produced by Saqib Saleem under the newly launched Saleem Siblings banner, Baby Do Die Do is positioned as a neo-noir crime thriller that blends satire with emotional turmoil. Think Monica, O My Darling meets something out of a Park Chan-wook fever dream — except set in small-town Maharashtra with a heroine who communicates through silence and violence.

"Baby Do Die Do isn't just the story of Baby KarMarKar — it's the story of an entire world that exists around her. Every character brings a distinct energy to the narrative, and this is only the beginning of what awaits audiences." — Director Nachiket Samant

The ensemble is quietly stacked. Chunky Panday and Sikandar Kher round out the cast — Kher reuniting with Huma after Monica, O My Darling and with Saqib after Citadel: Hunny Bunny. He described Samant as "clear about what he wants but not rigid," which is filmmaker shorthand for this person actually has a vision. That confidence shows in the teaser's texture: moody colour grading, rain-soaked frames, and a refusal to explain too much too soon.

But here's where the plot thickens outside the plot. Baby Do Die Do releases July 3, 2026. That's the exact same day Alia Bhatt and Sharvari's Alpha — the first female-led entry in the YRF Spy Universe — arrives in theatres with the full artillery of Yash Raj Films behind it. Two films about lethal women. Two completely different approaches. One opening weekend.

Alpha comes armed with a franchise machine built on Pathaan, Tiger and War, a teaser dropping tomorrow, and two of the biggest female stars working today. Baby Do Die Do is an independent production with a fraction of the budget, no spy universe, and a lead character who can't even speak. On paper, this should be a mismatch. But independent cinema has a way of turning mismatch into mystique.

For Huma, this is a bet on the kind of filmmaking that usually gets edged out by the tentpoles. She's not backed by a studio machine — she's backed by her brother and a script that clearly demanded she disappear into someone unrecognisable. In a Filmfare Middle East interview earlier this year, she put it plainly: "I'm not trying to follow anyone's path. I'm just doing my own thing." July 3 is where that philosophy meets the marketplace.

For diaspora audiences, the question is availability. Alpha will almost certainly command the wider release footprint across US, UK and Canada multiplexes. But if the Huma Qureshi of Gangs of Wasseypur and Monica, O My Darling is any guide, Baby Do Die Do is exactly the kind of film that becomes a cult streaming discovery three months later — the one you text your group chat about at 1 AM because you can't believe what you just watched.

Saqib Saleem, producing his sister's passion project through their shared banner, described the film as born from a desire to tell stories "for the newer generations" that are "a bit more edgy and new-age." Every frame of the teaser suggests they meant it.

Two assassins. One date. The only question is which one you see first.
